description: Range elements are filtering syntax used after the 'range' keyword in FLAC commands. They select subsets of model objects based on geometric regions, attributes, or logical conditions.

examples: structure node fix velocity range cylinder end-1 0 0 0 end-2 0 0 10 radius 5
notes: Multiple range elements create intersection (AND) by default
Unspecified range affects all objects of target type

live_verification.method: Every documented example was executed against a 216-point lattice with hand-checkable coordinates, and the number of material points each range matched was compared with the count computed by hand. This category had been inherited from FLAC by assumption -- the elements are kernel-level, but nothing had confirmed what they select on material points, which are not zones.
live_verification.result: All 22 documented elements parse, and every geometric and attribute element selects exactly the predicted set. One documented example is rejected by the engine ('range fish' quoting), one is a no-op on material points ('by'), and four useful elements were undocumented.
notes: 'range' may appear only once in a command: 'range position-x 0 20 range position-y 0 20' is rejected. Multiple elements go inside the single range phrase.
'extent' is meaningful on material points rather than a no-op -- they carry a volume, so 'sphere center (0,0,0) radius 0.7 extent' matched 0 where the same sphere without 'extent' matched 32.

Group slots hold ONE group per point. Assigning a second group in the same slot silently replaces the first, and the replaced group then matches nothing -- the original 'Group X assigned to 108 MPoints' message gives no hint that it will be superseded. Groups in different slots coexist.
Group names must be quoted: 'range group sample' is rejected, 'range group \'sample\'' works.

counts.expected: one (x,y) on the boundary exactly, all z -- boundary is inclusive

mpoint_additional_elements.name: volume
mpoint_additional_elements.description: Filter by material-point volume. Verified discriminating: 0..0.05 matched 0 points, 0.06..0.07 matched all 216, 0.07..1 matched 0, on a lattice whose point volume is exactly 0.4^3 = 0.064.

mpoint_additional_elements.name: velocity
mpoint_additional_elements.description: Filter by velocity magnitude. Verified discriminating at a 1e-12 threshold.

mpoint_additional_elements.name: displacement
mpoint_additional_elements.description: Filter by displacement magnitude. Verified discriminating at a 1e-12 threshold.

mpoint_additional_elements.name: selected / deselected
mpoint_additional_elements.description: Filter by GUI selection state. Both parse and evaluate, but there is no 'mpoint select' command, so selection can only be driven from the GUI.

mpoint_inapplicable_elements.name: by
mpoint_inapplicable_elements.reason: Its object-type list (ball, zone, clump, structure, ...) has no 'mpoint' entry, and 'by zone' / 'by ball' on an mpoint command parse but change the result by nothing. The shared doc's example 'range position-z 0 10 by zone' is a no-op here.

mpoint_inapplicable_elements.name: cmodel
mpoint_inapplicable_elements.reason: Matched 0 points even with every point assigned 'elastic'; it filters zone models.

mpoint_inapplicable_elements.name: radius
mpoint_inapplicable_elements.reason: Material points have no radius (a ball/pebble attribute). Always 0.
